scope: INFRA-156's own pull request carries root spec v16 R3 and A3 only: a typed block attribute of kind block[] that points at blocks, makes graph links named by the attribute, and limits the block types it points at. Every other requirement belongs to the children INFRA-364, 366, 367, 368, 369, 370, 371. Version 2 of the plan document is the plan of 2026-10-25 re-read against INFRA-366's pull request head (sjawhar/legion#2210 at c11366b53b43) and main 4d3fe8916fa8, with every place the code contradicted it corrected.
gate: The implementer starts coding only after dispatch://INFRA-366 (sjawhar/legion#2210) has merged to main. Until then it tells the architect (notifications.role.legion-infra-infra-156-architect) that the surface it needs is not on main yet and waits; the architect says when to continue. Then it brings main at or after INFRA-366's merge commit (gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/pulls/2210 --jq .merge_commit_sha) into the issue branch (no code or PR exists yet), re-reads every site the plan marks (366) at that commit, records each name mapping in the PR body, and reports to the architect before coding any shape the merged code lacks.
decisions: D1: the edge kind is the attribute's own name (serves -> serves); a block[] attribute name matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ and is not a structural edge kind (model.GraphEdgeKinds).
D2: the limit is a targets list of block type names (a typed type of the same schema, or a built-in type GET /blocks lists); absent means any.

D3: an agent/API write is refused (400 INVALID_MARKDOWN, or INVALID_OP field attributes on the edits route) when a pointer it introduces names an existing block of a disallowed type, resolved against the tree the write leaves for the same document and document_blocks otherwise; nil prior tree means every pointer is introduced; an absent target is accepted; a browser write and the reconciliation are never refused; block-aware reads list a pointer edge only while no current document_blocks row of its target has a disallowed type (block_refs.to_types plus SQL function block_ref_listed, not-exists form), an absent target falling to INFRA-366's never-listed rule; the index refreshes to_types on kept rows.
D4: a pinned pointer is limited by its target's current type.

D5: a pointer and a prose citation of one target are separate edges; the typed block's own mentions pair is subtracted for its pointer values; pointers from blocks that are not graph nodes write no row; heldByABlock drops its same-kind condition so the citing document's whole-document mentions edge never shows beside or instead of a pointer edge.
D6: ?kind= accepts schema-declared block[] names; the structural list moves from refs.Kinds to model.GraphEdgeKinds; block-links gains no ?kind=.

D7: document-level reads that never looked at blocks (GET /artifacts/{id}/references, the issue closure) keep listing the citing document as a mentions of every pointer target, allowed or hidden, because the value is a reference in the document's text; no dashboard page changes.

D8: the editor's typed-block commands refuse non-canonical values and a same-document target of a disallowed type, given a new documentRef option that ProofDocument sets to buildDispatchReference(documentRoute(artifact)), unversioned; markdown and HTML loading check canonical form only.

D9: a block[] value is empty or canonical dispatch:// block references joined by exactly one space, no repeats, refused otherwise (never normalised); canonical = parse then text.FormatBlockRef equals the value (issue primary document as /spec, project documents always artifact/<slug>, pin 1..MaxInt64 without leading zero); the value table is a @legion/contracts constant with a generated Go JSON copy checked by a contracts test (INFRA-366's encodings-table pattern), and proof-editor imports contracts instead of keeping a twin.
tasks: Task 1: text.FormatBlockRef and text.CanonicalBlockRef; block[] kind in the Go schema (model.GraphEdgeKinds, pmdoc schema targets/validation/ParseBlockPointerValue/render, LinkKinds, UseBlockSchemaForTest(t, schema) restoring on t.Cleanup, ?kind= acceptance) with schema tests.
Task 2: pmdoc.BlockPointers and CheckBlockPointers; refuse disallowed targets in applyLive (before it releases the starting tree), SeedText and RebuildDocument with 400s; pure and HTTP tests.

Task 3: migration <N> (0123 if nothing lands after INFRA-366) up.sql plus census.sql (select 0), no down.sql, no key change: block_refs.to_types, block_ref_listed (not-exists form), restated graph_edges arm; readEdgeRows and BlockLinks apply it; heldByABlock any kind; IndexBlocks takes pointers, keeps only node-set sources, insert refreshes to_types on conflict; indexVersion derives pointers (none when LinkKinds is empty or no blocks, tree when given, else ParseRendering with warn-and-skip on error); HTTP, settlement, targets-change, reconciliation-parity and EXPLAIN tests.

Task 4: contracts parseCanonicalBlockReference, formatBlockReference, parseBlockPointerValue, DISPATCH_BLOCK_POINTER_VALUES with Go copy check; contracts types (block[], targets, open GraphEdgeKind); proof-editor depends on @legion/contracts (package.json, bun.lock), own file block-pointers.ts added to biome.json's override exceptions, block-schema.ts, typed-block-commands.ts, lib.ts documentRef; ProofDocument passes documentRef; proof-editor AGENTS.md sixteenth kind of edit, ten own files, Conventions; editor and contracts tests.

Task 5: docs (packages/envoy/AGENTS.md typed-block, edge-kind, heldByABlock and refs.Kinds lines; cmd/dispatch README and AGENTS edge kinds and the new migration; contracts AGENTS) and changelogs (envoy, contracts).

proof.implementer: Throwaway $TMPDIR/a3-e2e.sh at the head: a scratch blocks.json adding requirement and claim (serves: block[], targets [requirement]) present only while bun run dispatch:local builds the server (schema is go:embed), then restored with jj restore; drive the real server over HTTP and with bun packages/envoy-client/bin/dispatch.ts (DISPATCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8777, DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token): a claim pointing at requirement r1 saves and dispatch read of r1 shows a serves edge; ?kind=serves lists it; negative controls: a pointer to a paragraph or a callout is 400 naming the types, a malformed, over-encoded or artifact/spec-spelled value is 400 INVALID_MARKDOWN, ?kind=nope is 400 INVALID_KIND, serves="" removes the edge.
proof.tester: Re-run the script at the head under test and try to break it: pointer added by edit op, target added in the same upload, retype of the target to callout and back (edge hidden then shown), pinned pointer, doubled space, tab or leading space in a value (each 400 INVALID_MARKDOWN); read CI for static lanes.
proof.production: No shipped type declares block[] (R3), so production cannot exercise the new path. The check records that the running build carries the merge (dispatch-production-check.sh --commit <merge sha> --page /issues --route /api/v1/references --route /api/v1/schema/blocks), that the served schema has no block[] attribute, that a callout document uploads and a block reference to it reads as before on a LEGSMOKE scratch issue, and that ?kind=mentions answers and ?kind=nope is still 400; the Production: line says the new path is unreachable in production until INFRA-173 ships a type that declares one.

findings.finding: F1: every pointer value is also a whole-document mentions on GET /artifacts/{id}/references and the issue closure, which read refs without heldByABlock or to_types; the old plan's D3/D7 claimed otherwise.
findings.answer: Accepted as the design (D7): the value is a reference in the document's text, so those document-level reads list the citing document as a mention, allowed or hidden; D3 and D7 rewritten, and TestABlockPointerIsListedOnlyWhileItsTargetHasAnAllowedType asserts the legacy route still lists the spec under outgoing while the pointer is hidden. Reported to the architect as a how-to-build call it may overrule.

findings.finding: F2: INFRA-366's insert does nothing on conflict, so a kept pair never gets a new to_types and a targets change never reaches stored rows.
findings.answer: Task 3 step 4: on conflict do update set to_types = excluded.to_types where distinct, the pair's target returned as moved; TestATargetsChangeReachesStoredPointersAtTheNextIndexing.

findings.finding: F3: pointers from blocks that are not graph nodes, a ParseRendering failure on the reconciliation path, and no check that the write path and reconciliation path store the same rows.
findings.answer: IndexBlocks keeps only pointers whose source is in its node set; a ParseRendering error logs a warning and indexes with no pointers, as the reconciliation already does for an unreadable document; TestTheReconciliationIndexesTheSamePointersAsTheVersionWrite compares block_refs rows after a version write and after ReconcileBlockIndex.

findings.finding: F4: the canonical writer rule must key on IssueKey (project documents may have slug spec), refuse non-block kinds, and agree with TS on pin bounds; the corpus lacked these rows.
findings.answer: Task 1 step 1 defines text.FormatBlockRef and CanonicalBlockRef with those rules; Task 4 step 1 adds the rows (artifact/spec refused for an issue, accepted for a project, bare document, agent document, largest pin, pin past it, @v01, @v0, 256-byte and longer ids); the TS twin is contracts' formatBlockReference.

findings.finding: F5: whitespace inside a value could be normalised or refused, and JS and Go disagree on what whitespace is.
findings.answer: D9 picks refuse: the value must be the single-space join exactly; corpus rows for a doubled, leading and trailing space, a tab and U+FEFF; the tester's break attempts expect 400 INVALID_MARKDOWN.

findings.finding: F6: contracts has only the fragment half, so the editor still needs the document grammar; the dependency, bun.lock, biome.json override and AGENTS.md chores were unlisted.
findings.answer: The whole canonical parser and writer live once in TS, in contracts' dispatch-block-ref.ts beside the table; proof-editor imports them; Task 4 lists package.json, bun.lock, the biome.json exception for block-pointers.ts, and AGENTS.md (ten own files, sixteen kinds at :48 and :85, Conventions).

findings.finding: F7: a deferred schema restore runs before t.Cleanup's server Shutdown, so room and settlement goroutines could read the restored schema (a data race under envoy-go-race).
findings.answer: UseBlockSchemaForTest(t, schema) registers its restore with t.Cleanup and is called before any server or service is built, so it runs after Shutdown; the targets-change test swaps a second schema only with no room open.

findings.finding: F8: applyLive releases its starting tree at docs/mutation.go:184 (366) and has none when the starting tree is outside the schema.
findings.answer: Task 2 step 4 calls CheckBlockPointers before that release; a nil prior counts every pointer as introduced, tested in TestCheckBlockPointersRefusesATargetOfADisallowedType.

findings.finding: F9: document_blocks.node_id is not unique, so a scalar subquery could error; a function with a subquery may not be inlined, so the view's EXPLAIN cannot see its lookup.
findings.answer: block_ref_listed uses the not-exists form; graph_edges_test adds an EXPLAIN of the function's own query with enable_seqscan off expecting the node_id index.

findings.finding: F10: dropping heldByABlock's same-kind condition changes INFRA-366's documented rule in refs/graph.go comments and packages/envoy/AGENTS.md.
findings.answer: Task 3 step 3 updates both comments; Task 5 updates the AGENTS.md sentence; the listing test keeps the regression assertion that no whole-document mentions appears while a pointer row exists, hidden or not.

findings.finding: F11: the rolling-deploy hazard is wider than INFRA-366 versus this PR: any build that cannot read a new typed type, or declares no block[] attribute, deletes pointer rows on its next index.
findings.answer: Risks rewritten: this PR ships no block[] type so no pointer row exists in production; the change that first ships one (INFRA-173) owns the hazard and runs rebuild-refs after its roll. Reported to the architect.

findings.finding: F12: citation and wording corrections (documentRef builder, absent-target wording, D6 import reasoning, node_id uniqueness, parallel tests, Task 5 doc sites, review grep rule, ReplaceCountedRefs name).
findings.answer: All applied in plan document version 2: D8 names buildDispatchReference(documentRoute(artifact)); D3 says an absent target is never listed; D6 reasoning corrected; Risks corrected; Task 5 lists the refs.Kinds bullet, the heldByABlock sentence, the migration paragraph and keeps README :850-853; the review rule greps non-test files and names the allowed hits.
